recent_posts.title: JavaScript source maps
recent_posts.summary: Gleam v1.16.0 has been released with several notable improvements. The headline feature is JavaScript source map support, enabling browsers and runtimes to map compiled JS back to original Gleam code for debugging, breakpoints, and stack traces. Other highlights include package-level fault tolerance in the compiler (so unrelated modules still compile when one fails), ~30% faster string pattern matching on the JavaScript target, new language server code actions (add/remove anonymous functions, extract function improvements, replace type holes), oversized int pattern warnings for JavaScript's 52-bit limit, constant list prepending, and improved tuple formatting.

recent_posts.title: Upgrading Hex security
recent_posts.summary: Gleam v1.15.0 has been released with a major security upgrade: the build tool now exclusively uses Hex's new OAuth2-based authentication system, replacing legacy username/password tokens. Key benefits include mandatory MFA for write operations, short-lived tokens, and password-less client authentication. Other highlights include improved Hex error messages, guard clause ergonomics (string concatenation in guards), JavaScript FFI additions for BitArray, package quality checks requiring a non-default README, code folding support in the language server, improved CLI documentation, snake_case consistency in gleam.toml, and numerous language server improvements including extract anonymous function, module usage renaming, missing type parameter code actions, and more precise completions.

recent_posts.title: Join us at Gleam Gathering
recent_posts.summary: Gleam Gathering, the first dedicated Gleam programming language conference, takes place February 21st in Bristol, UK. The event features talks from community members and core team on topics like compiler optimization, networking opportunities, and post-conference activities at a retro-games arcade. Last-minute tickets are still available.

recent_posts.title: Formalising external APIs
recent_posts.summary: Gleam v1.13.0 introduces formalized external APIs for JavaScript interop, allowing safer integration with external code through dedicated functions for constructing and accessing Gleam data types. The release includes significant compiler improvements: enhanced bit array exhaustiveness checking with interference-based pruning, unused argument detection in recursive functions, and better fault-tolerant analysis. The language server gains multiple new code actions including extract function, collapse nested cases, and pattern matching helpers. Additional improvements include better error messages for common syntax mistakes from other languages, dependency version change notifications, and enhanced type display in documentation.

recent_posts.title: Gleam v1.12.0 improves dependency management and developer experience
recent_posts.summary: Gleam v1.12.0 introduces significant improvements to dependency management with clearer conflict resolution error messages, major version update notifications, and enhanced debugging capabilities. The release includes code generation optimizations that reduce output size, better list formatting control in the automatic formatter, JSDoc support for JavaScript compilation, and various developer experience enhancements like improved error messages and language server features.

recent_posts.title: Gleam JavaScript gets 30% faster
recent_posts.summary: Gleam v1.11.0 introduces significant performance improvements with 30% faster JavaScript compilation through optimized pattern matching using decision trees instead of linear if-else chains. The release adds new testing capabilities with built-in assert syntax, a dedicated dev/ directory for development code accessible via 'gleam dev' command, and enhanced language server features including better code actions and fault tolerance. Additional improvements include JavaScript bit array support for UTF-16/UTF-32, better documentation generation, and various developer experience enhancements.

recent_posts.title: Global rename and find references
recent_posts.summary: Gleam v1.10.0 introduces several enhancements including the project-wide call reference graph, improved exhaustiveness analysis, better binary operator analysis, and support for new bit array literal features. It also boosts JavaScript code generation performance, offers more robust cross-platform deployment artifacts, and introduces various new code actions for the language server. Additionally, there are significant improvements for security and compliance with the inclusion of Software Bill of Materials (SBoM) and SLSA Provenance information.

recent_posts.title: Hello echo! Hello git!
recent_posts.summary: Gleam v1.9.0 introduces several new features and enhancements including the Echo debug printing, allowing values to be printed with file path and line number, and support for Git dependencies. Other updates include improvements to bit arrays and list pattern matching in JavaScript, go-to type definition functionality, HexDocs search integration, support for custom CA certificates, and various code actions like generating JSON encoders and multi-variant decoders.

recent_posts.title: Gleam gets "rename variable"
recent_posts.summary: Gleam v1.8.0 has been released with several new features and improvements. Key additions include the ability to rename variables and function arguments in the language server, integration of Erlang OTP27 documentation, automatic function definition generation, pattern match suggestions, and enhanced fault-tolerant compilation. There are also improvements in error handling hints, the introduction of a new `gleam deps tree` command to visualize dependencies, hotkeys for HTML documentation, and better handling of invalid project names.

recent_posts.title: Developer Survey 2024 Results
recent_posts.summary: The first Gleam Developer Survey received 841 responses, showing significant adoption of the Gleam programming language. A majority of respondents use Gleam, with a notable percentage having it in production. The survey covers participant demographics, their Gleam usage, other programming languages they use, and highlights areas for improvement in Gleam like JSON decoding, OTP actor framework, and better documentation. Despite challenges in corporate sponsorship, community support remains strong.

top_posts.title: Welcome Lambda! – Gleam
top_posts.summary: Lambda, a diverse tech company involved in machine learning, crypto infrastructure, video games, and animation, has become the primary sponsor of Gleam, a type-safe and scalable language for Erlang VM and JavaScript runtimes. Lambda utilizes various BEAM languages and has an extensive open-source portfolio, including their latest mobile game, Champions of Mirra. They plan to use Gleam for future backend iterations, underscoring their commitment to the Gleam ecosystem.

top_posts.title: Introducing the Gleam roadmap!
top_posts.summary: Gleam's project leader, Louis Pilfold, introduces a development roadmap for the Gleam programming language. This roadmap will provide an overview of impactful features, past, present, and future, and will be updated regularly. It aims to offer a quicker way for the community to access information about Gleam's progress.
